title: Pāṇini measures a vowel
source_body: Pāṇini names vowels by how long they last. In sūtra 1.2.27 a vowel lasting as long as {{उ}} is {{ह्रस्वः}}, short; as long as {{ऊ}}, {{दीर्घः}}, long; held for three beats, {{प्लुतः}}. All five vowels of the leaf's first two groups are {{ह्रस्वः}}.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Twins in Pāṇini
source_body: Sūtra 1.1.9 calls sounds made at one place with one effort {{सवर्ण}}, “of one kind”: {{इ}} and {{ई}} are {{सवर्ण}}. By sūtra 1.1.69 a short vowel in a rule stands for its twins too. So the leaf, like Pāṇini's list, writes only {{अ}} {{इ}} {{उ}}, never {{आ}} {{ई}} {{ऊ}}.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's names for these vowels
source_body: The first two sūtras of the Aṣṭādhyāyī name vowels you now know. {{आ}} {{ऐ}} {{औ}} are {{वृद्धि}} (1.1.1); {{अ}} {{ए}} {{ओ}} are {{गुण}} (1.1.2). Many later rules say “becomes guṇa” or “becomes vṛddhi”, and when words join you will watch these vowels appear.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: The row names
source_body: Pāṇini names each row by its first letter plus {{उ}}: {{कु}} is the throat row, {{चु}} the palate row, {{टु}} the roof row, {{तु}} the teeth row, {{पु}} the lip row. By sūtra 1.1.69 a letter with {{उ}} stands for its whole row.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's name for them
source_body: Pāṇini's Śiva sūtras 5 and 6 are {{हयवरट्}} and {{लण्}}. Drop the marker letters {{ट्}} and {{ण्}}, and {{य}} {{व}} {{र}} {{ल}} remain. He calls this group {{यण्}}: from {{य}} up to the marker {{ण्}}.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's names
source_body: The Śiva sūtra {{शषसर्}} (13) ends in the marker {{र्}}; {{हल्}} (14) ends in {{ल्}}. From {{श}} to that {{ल्}} Pāṇini's group {{शल्}} holds exactly {{श}} {{ष}} {{स}} {{ह}}. And {{हल्}}, from the {{ह}} of sūtra 5, is every consonant.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's rule for the hum
source_body: Sūtra 8.3.23, {{मोऽनुस्वारः}}: a final {{म्}} before a consonant becomes the dot. So {{रामम्}} + {{नमति}} is written {{रामं नमति}}.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: The test for ‘same kind’
source_body: Sūtra 1.1.9 says sounds with the same place and the same effort are {{सवर्ण}}, of one kind: {{इ}} and {{ई}} differ only in length; {{क}} and {{ख}} share a place but not an effort.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's definition of a word
source_body: Sūtra 1.4.14, {{सुप्तिङन्तं पदम्}}: a word ({{पदम्}}) is what ends in a noun ending ({{सुप्}}) or a verb ending ({{तिङ्}}). So {{बालकः}} and {{पठति}} are words; the bare stems {{बालक}} and {{पठ्}} are not yet.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's doer
source_body: Sūtra 1.4.54, {{स्वतन्त्रः कर्ता}}, calls the doer “the independent one”: the one who is free to act. Sūtra 2.3.46 says the first case shows the bare meaning of the word.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini on number
source_body: Sūtra 1.4.22, {{द्व्येकयोर्द्विवचनैकवचने}}: the dual ending goes with two things, the singular with one. Number is a feature of the ending, not of the stem.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Why {{पत्राणि}}, not {{पत्रानि}}?
source_body: After {{र}}, {{ऋ}} or {{ष}}, a following {{न}} becomes {{ण}}, even across vowels. That is why {{पत्र}} has {{पत्राणि}} but {{फल}} has {{फलानि}}. You will meet this again in the sandhi chapters.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: The first person in Pāṇini
source_body: Pāṇini calls the “I” person {{उत्तमः}}, “the highest”, and the “you” person {{मध्यमः}}, “the middle”. The “he, she, it” person, which you know already, is {{प्रथमः}}, “the first”. The names go in an order opposite to Hindi's.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's feminine makers
source_body: Sūtra 4.1.4 says a word ending in {{अ}} makes its feminine with {{टाप्}}, which shows up as {{आ}}. Sūtra 4.1.5 gives {{ङीप्}}, which shows up as {{ई}}, to words in {{ऋ}} and {{न्}} and others.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's object
source_body: Sūtra 1.4.49, {{कर्तुरीप्सिततमं कर्म}}, calls the object “what the doer most wishes to reach”. Sūtra 2.3.2, {{कर्मणि द्वितीया}}, puts it in the second case.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's tool
source_body: Sūtra 1.4.42, {{साधकतमं करणम्}}, calls the tool “the most effective means” of an action. Sūtra 2.3.18 puts the tool, and the doer of a passive verb, in the third case.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: {{सह}} or {{सार्धम्}}
source_body: {{सह}} may be replaced by {{सार्धम्}} or {{साकम्}} with the same meaning, and the third case can even stand alone: {{मित्रेण गच्छामि}}. Poets use all of these freely.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's recipient
source_body: Sūtra 1.4.32, {{कर्मणा यमभिप्रैति स सम्प्रदानम्}}: the recipient is the one the doer aims at with the object. Sūtra 2.3.13 gives it the fourth case.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's source
source_body: Sūtra 1.4.24, {{ध्रुवमपायेऽपादानम्}}: when two things move apart, the fixed one is the source. A leaf falls from a tree; the tree stays. Sūtra 2.3.28 gives the source the fifth case.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's “rest”
source_body: Sūtra 2.3.50, {{षष्ठी शेषे}}, gives the sixth case to “the rest”: every link between two nouns that the other kāraka-cases do not express. That is why it covers owner, part, kin and more.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's locus
source_body: Sūtra 1.4.45, {{आधारोऽधिकरणम्}}: the locus is the support. Sūtra 2.3.36, {{सप्तम्यधिकरणे च}}: it takes the seventh case.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: “When that happens”
source_body: A seventh-case word can also say “while this was happening”. It is the “absolute” construction, {{सति सप्तमी}}, and you will meet it in the syntax chapter.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's address
source_body: Sūtra 2.3.47, {{सम्बोधने च}}, gives address the first case in form, and 2.3.49, {{एकवचनं सम्बुद्धिः}}, names the singular ending of the call {{सम्बुद्धिः}}. So the call is a special form of the first case.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Why {{देवैः}}?
source_body: Pāṇini's sūtra 7.1.9, {{अतो भिस ऐस्}}, changes the ending {{भिस्}} to {{ऐस्}} after a word in -{{अ}}: {{देव}} + {{भिस्}} → {{देवैः}}. And 7.1.12 turns {{टा}} into {{इन}}, {{ङसि}} into {{आत्}} and {{ङस्}} into {{स्य}}: {{देवेन}}, {{देवात्}}, {{देवस्य}}.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's guṇa
source_body: Why {{कवयः}} and not {{कविः}} again? Sūtra 7.3.109, {{जसि च}}, strengthens a final {{इ}}/{{उ}} to {{ए}}/{{ओ}} before the plural ending {{जस्}}; and {{ए}} becomes {{अय्}} before a vowel. In the singular call, 6.1.69, {{एङ्ह्रस्वात् सम्बुद्धेः}}, drops the ending after {{ए}}.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's {{ऋ}}
source_body: Sūtra 7.3.110, {{ऋतो ङिसर्वनामस्थानयोः}}, gives {{ऋ}} its strong form {{अर्}} before {{ङि}} and the strong endings: {{पितरि}}, {{पितरौ}}, {{पितरः}}. Sūtra 7.1.94 makes the first singular {{पिता}} by turning {{ऋ}} into {{अन्}} and lengthening.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's pronoun rules
source_body: Sūtra 7.2.102, {{त्यदादीनामः}}, makes the stem {{तद्}} end in {{अ}}; 7.2.106, {{तदोः सः सावनन्त्ययोः}}, turns its {{त्}} into {{स्}} before the first-case ending, giving {{सः}}. Then 7.1.14, {{सर्वनाम्नः स्मै}}, gives {{तस्मै}}; 7.1.15, {{ङसिङ्योः स्मात्स्मिनौ}}, gives {{तस्मात्}} and {{तस्मिन्}}; 7.1.17, {{जसः शी}}, gives {{ते}}; and 7.1.52, {{आमि सर्वनाम्नः सुट्}}, gives {{तेषाम्}}.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's command
source_body: Sūtra 3.3.162, {{लोट् च}}, gives {{लोट्}} for commands and requests. Then 3.4.86, {{एरुः}}, turns {{-ति}} into {{-तु}}: {{पठतु}}. In the second person {{हि}} comes and 6.4.105, {{अतो हेः}}, drops it after {{अ}}: {{पठ}}. In the first person 3.4.92, {{आडुत्तमस्य पिच्च}}, adds {{आ}}: {{पठानि}}.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's past
source_body: Sūtra 3.2.111, {{अनद्यतने लङ्}}, gives {{लङ्}} for a past not of today. 6.4.71, {{लुङ्लङ्लृङ्क्ष्वडुदात्तः}}, adds the augment {{अ}}. Then 3.4.100, {{इतश्च}}, drops the final {{-इ}} of the ending {{-ति}}, so {{-ति}} becomes {{-त्}}: {{अपठत्}}.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's future
source_body: Sūtra 3.3.13, {{लृट् शेषे च}}, gives {{लृट्}} for what will happen. 3.1.33, {{स्यतासी लृलुटोः}}, adds {{स्य}}. 7.2.35, {{आर्धधातुकस्येड् वलादेः}}, adds {{इ}} before a consonant, so {{पठ् + इ + स्य}}; and 8.3.59, {{आदेशप्रत्यययोः}}, turns {{स्}} into {{ष्}} after {{इ}}: {{पठिष्यति}}.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's “should”
source_body: Sūtra 3.3.161, {{विधिनिमन्त्रणामन्त्रणाधीष्टसंप्रश्नप्रार्थनेषु लिङ्}}, gives {{लिङ्}} for advice, invitation and request. 3.4.103, {{यासुट् परस्मैपदेषूदात्तो ङिच्च}}, adds {{यास्}}; 7.2.80, {{अतो येयः}}, makes {{या}} into {{इय्}}; 6.1.87, {{आद्गुणः}}, joins {{अ + इ}} into {{ए}}: {{पठेत्}}.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's doubling
source_body: Sūtra 3.2.115, {{परोक्षे लिट्}}, gives {{लिट्}} for the unseen past. 6.1.8, {{लिटि धातोरनभ्यासस्य}}, and 6.1.1, {{एकाचो द्वे प्रथमस्य}}, double the root. 7.4.62, {{कुहोश्चुः}}, turns a guttural in the doubled part into a palatal: {{ग}} becomes {{ज}}, giving {{जगाम}}.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's aorist
source_body: Sūtra 3.2.110, {{लुङ्}}, gives the aorist for what is past. 3.1.43, {{च्लि लुङि}}, puts {{च्लि}} before it, and 3.1.44, {{च्लेः सिच्}}, turns it into {{सिच्}}. 7.2.1, {{सिचि वृद्धिः परस्मैपदेषु}}, lengthens the root vowel, so {{कृ}} becomes {{कार्}}: {{अकार्षीत्}}.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's {{मा}}
source_body: Sūtra 3.3.175, {{माङि लुङ्}}, says that after {{मा}} the {{लुङ्}} is used. And 6.4.74, {{न माङ्योगे}}, says the augment {{अ}} does not appear when {{मा}} is attached. So {{अगमः}} becomes {{मा गमः}}.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: The rules behind the rare forms
source_body: {{लुट्}} places an action beyond today. {{आशीर्लिङ्}} expresses a blessing. {{लृङ्}} describes an action that did not come about when its condition failed. These rules explain the three forms in the table; {{लेट्}} belongs to Vedic usage.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's class sign
source_body: Sūtra 3.1.68, {{कर्तरि शप्}}, adds {{शप्}} (which leaves {{अ}}) after a root when the doer is named. 7.3.84, {{सार्वधातुकार्धधातुकयोः}}, strengthens the root's last vowel: {{भू}} becomes {{भो}}. Then 6.1.78, {{एचोऽयवायावः}}, makes {{ओ}} before a vowel into {{अव्}}: {{भवति}}.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's {{-य-}}
source_body: Sūtra 3.1.69, {{दिवादिभ्यः श्यन्}}, adds {{श्यन्}} after the roots of {{दिव्}} and its class; the {{श्}} and {{न्}} drop away and leave {{-य-}}. Because this sign is not the strengthening kind, the root keeps its own vowel: {{नृत्यति}}, not {{नर्त्यति}}.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's unstrengthened sign
source_body: Sūtra 3.1.77, {{तुदादिभ्यः शः}}, adds {{श}} after {{तुद्}} and its class. This sign is {{ङित्}}, “marked”, and 1.1.5, {{क्ङिति च}}, forbids the strengthening before a marked sign: {{तुदति}}. And 7.3.77, {{इषुगमियमां छः}}, turns {{इष्}}, {{गम्}} and {{यम्}} into {{इच्छ्}}, {{गच्छ्}}, {{यच्छ्}}.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's {{णिच्}}
source_body: Sūtra 3.1.25, {{सत्यापपाशरूपवीणातूलश्लोकसेनालोमत्वचवर्मवर्णचूर्णचुरादिभ्यो णिच्}}, adds {{णिच्}}, which becomes {{-इ-}} and then {{-अय-}}. 7.3.86, {{पुगन्तलघूपधस्य च}}, strengthens a short middle vowel: {{चुर्}} becomes {{चोर्}}. So {{चोर + अय + ति}}: {{चोरयति}}.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's no-sign class
source_body: Sūtra 2.4.72, {{अदिप्रभृतिभ्यः शपः}}, deletes the sign {{शप्}} after {{अद्}} and its class, so the ending joins the root. 6.4.111, {{श्नसोरल्लोपः}}, drops the {{अ}} of {{अस्}} before a weak ending: {{स्तः}}, {{सन्ति}}.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's doubling class
source_body: Sūtra 2.4.75, {{जुहोत्यादिभ्यः श्लुः}}, replaces the sign {{शप्}} with {{श्लु}}, which is deleted but leaves the root doubled. 6.1.10, {{श्लौ}}, orders the doubling. And 7.4.58, {{अत्र लोपोऽभ्यासस्य}}, shortens the doubled start, giving {{दद-}}.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's {{नु}} and {{उ}}
source_body: Sūtra 3.1.73, {{स्वादिभ्यः श्नुः}}, adds {{श्नु}} to class 5, and 3.1.79, {{तनादिकृञ्भ्य उः}}, adds {{उ}} to class 8 and to {{कृ}}. And 3.1.74, {{श्रुवः शृ च}}, gives {{श्रु}} the {{श्नु}} sign and turns it into {{शृ}}: {{शृणोति}}.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's two signs
source_body: Sūtra 3.1.78, {{रुधादिभ्यः श्नम्}}, puts the infix {{श्नम्}} inside the root of class 7: {{रुध् + न + ध्}}. 3.1.81, {{क्र्यादिभ्यः श्ना}}, adds {{श्ना}} to class 9, which gives {{-ना-}}; and 6.4.112, {{श्नाऽभ्यस्तयोरातः}}, drops its {{आ}} before a weak ending: {{जानीतः}}.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's two sets
source_body: Sūtra 1.4.99, {{लः परस्मैपदम्}}, and 1.4.100, {{तङानावात्मनेपदम्}}, name the two sets; the second is the {{तङ्}} endings. 1.3.12, {{अनुदात्तङित आत्मनेपदम्}}, says roots with a marked sign take the second set. And 3.4.79, {{टित आत्मनेपदानां टेरे}}, turns the end of {{-त}} into {{-ते}}.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's choice
source_body: Sūtra 1.3.72, {{स्वरितञितः कर्त्रभिप्राये क्रियाफले}}, says the second set is used when the fruit of the action goes to the doer. And 1.3.78, {{शेषात् कर्तरि परस्मैपदम्}}, says that for all other roots the first set is the default. Prefixes can change the set; for example {{विपराभ्यां जेः}}, 1.3.19, gives {{विजयते}}.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's prefixes
source_body: Sūtra 1.4.59, {{उपसर्गाः क्रियायोगे}}, names words like {{प्र}} and {{परा}} as {{उपसर्ग}} when they join a verb. 1.4.80, {{ते प्राग्धातोः}}, says they stand before the root. Together they give {{आ + गच्छति}} = {{आगच्छति}}.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's list
source_body: Sūtra 1.4.58, {{प्रादयः}}, gives the list {{प्र}} onwards, and 1.4.59, {{उपसर्गाः क्रियायोगे}}, names those that join a verb {{उपसर्ग}}. The list of twenty-two is a tradition from the grammarians and is memorised as a verse.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's passive
source_body: Sūtra 3.4.69, {{लः कर्मणि च भावे चाकर्मकेभ्यः}}, says the verb endings can state the object, or the action itself for roots with no object. 3.1.67, {{सार्वधातुके यक्}}, adds {{यक्}}; and 1.3.13, {{भावकर्मणोः}}, gives the endings for oneself: {{पठ्यते}}.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's causative
source_body: Sūtra 3.1.26, {{हेतुमति च}}, adds {{णिच्}} when someone gets the action done. 7.2.115, {{अचो ञ्णिति}}, lengthens the root's vowel before it: {{पठ्}} becomes {{पाठ्}}. 3.1.32, {{सनाद्यन्ता धातवः}}, says the new stem is itself a root: {{पाठयति}}.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's wanting
source_body: Sūtra 3.1.7, {{धातोः कर्मणः समानकर्तृकादिच्छायां वा}}, gives {{सन्}} to a root when the same person wants to do the action. 6.1.9, {{सन्यङोः}}, orders the doubling, and 7.4.58, {{अत्र लोपोऽभ्यासस्य}}, shortens the first half. 7.2.35 adds the {{इ}}: {{पिपठिषति}}.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's “having done”
source_body: Sūtra 3.4.21, {{समानकर्तृकयोः पूर्वकाले}}, gives {{क्त्वा}} for an earlier action by the same doer. 7.1.37, {{समासेऽनञ्पूर्वे क्त्वो ल्यप्}}, turns {{क्त्वा}} into {{ल्यप्}}, that is {{-य}}, after a prefix. 1.1.40, {{क्त्वातोसुन्कसुनः}}, says these endings are indeclinable.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's purpose
source_body: Sūtra 3.3.10, {{तुमुन्ण्वुलौ क्रियायां क्रियार्थायाम्}}, gives {{तुमुन्}} when one action is for another action. And 3.3.158, {{समानकर्तृकेषु तुमुन्}}, gives it with verbs of wanting when the doer is the same.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's “done”
source_body: Sūtra 1.1.26, {{क्तक्तवतू निष्ठा}}, names {{क्त}} and {{क्तवतु}} {{निष्ठा}}, and 3.2.102, {{निष्ठा}}, gives them for the past. 3.4.70, {{तयोरेव कृत्यक्तखलर्थाः}}, says {{क्त}} is used for the object or the bare action, and 3.4.72, {{गत्यर्थाकर्मकश्लिषशीङ्स्थाऽऽसवसजनरुहजीर्यतिभ्यश्च}}, lets it be active for verbs of going: {{गतः}}.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's “while”
source_body: Sūtra 3.2.124, {{लटः शतृशानचावप्रथमासमानाधिकरणे}}, replaces the present endings with {{शतृ}} or {{शानच्}}, “while doing”, when the word is not in the first case with the verb. 7.1.78, {{नाभ्यस्ताच्छतुः}}, and 6.4.14, {{अत्वसन्तस्य चाधातोः}}, give the forms {{गच्छन्}} and {{गच्छत्}}.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's “ought”
source_body: Sūtra 3.1.96, {{तव्यत्तव्यानीयरः}}, gives {{तव्यत्}}, {{तव्य}} and {{अनीयर्}}; 3.1.97, {{अचो यत्}}, gives {{यत्}} after a root ending in a vowel, and 3.1.124, {{ऋहलोर्ण्यत्}}, gives {{ण्यत्}}. 3.4.70, {{तयोरेव कृत्यक्तखलर्थाः}}, says the “must” words state the object or the bare action.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's indeclinables
source_body: Sūtra 1.1.37, {{स्वरादिनिपातमव्ययम्}}, calls the words beginning with {{स्वर्}} and the particles {{निपात}}, “indeclinable”. 1.1.38, {{तद्धितश्चासर्वविभक्तिः}}, adds the {{तद्धित}} words that take no case ending. Because they are {{अव्यय}}, their case endings are deleted and they never change.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's {{इति}}
source_body: {{इति}} is a {{निपात}}, a particle, listed with {{च}} and {{वा}} in the grammarians' lists of {{चादि}}. By 1.4.57, {{चादयोऽसत्त्वे}}, it has the name {{निपात}} and, by 1.1.37, it is indeclinable.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's three endings
source_body: These words are made with {{तद्धित}} endings. 5.3.10, {{सप्तम्यास्त्रल्}}, makes {{-त्र}} (place); 5.3.15, {{सर्वैकान्यकिंयत्तदः काले दा}}, makes {{-दा}} (time); 5.3.23, {{प्रकारवचने थाल्}}, makes {{-था}} (manner). By 1.1.38 they take no case endings, so they are indeclinable.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's merging
source_body: Sūtra 6.1.101, {{अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः}}, says that when {{अ}}, {{इ}}, {{उ}} or {{ऋ}} (short or long) meets a vowel of its own family, the two become one long vowel. 1.1.9, {{तुल्यास्यप्रयत्नं सवर्णम्}}, defines “own family”: sounds made in the same place with the same effort.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's guṇa
source_body: Sūtra 6.1.87, {{आद्गुणः}}, says that after {{अ}} or {{आ}}, a following vowel merges with it into its guṇa. 1.1.2, {{अदेङ् गुणः}}, names {{अ}}, {{ए}}, {{ओ}} guṇa. So {{अ + इ}} gives {{ए}}, {{अ + उ}} gives {{ओ}}.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's growth
source_body: Sūtra 6.1.88, {{वृद्धिरेचि}}, says that when {{अ}} or {{आ}} meets an {{एच्}} vowel ({{ए}}, {{ओ}}, {{ऐ}}, {{औ}}) the result is vṛddhi. 1.1.1, {{वृद्धिरादैच्}}, names {{आ}}, {{ऐ}}, {{औ}} vṛddhi. So {{अ + ए}} gives {{ऐ}} and {{अ + ओ}} gives {{औ}}.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's glide
source_body: Sūtra 6.1.77, {{इको यणचि}}, says that {{इक्}} (the vowels {{इ}}, {{उ}}, {{ऋ}}, {{ऌ}}) is replaced by {{यण्}} ({{य्}}, {{व्}}, {{र्}}, {{ल्}}) before a vowel. So {{इति + आदि}} gives {{इत्यादि}}, {{सु + आगतम्}} gives {{स्वागतम्}}.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's ay, av
source_body: Sūtra 6.1.78, {{एचोऽयवायावः}}, replaces {{ए}}, {{ओ}}, {{ऐ}}, {{औ}} before a vowel with {{अय्}}, {{अव्}}, {{आय्}}, {{आव्}}. And 6.1.109, {{एङः पदान्तादति}}, says that a word-final {{ए}} or {{ओ}} before {{अ}} keeps itself and the {{अ}} is dropped, marked {{ऽ}}.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's closed door
source_body: Sūtra 1.1.11, {{ईदूदेद्द्विवचनं प्रगृह्यम्}}, names the dual forms ending in {{ई}}, {{ऊ}}, {{ए}} {{प्रगृह्य}}. And 6.1.125, {{प्लुतप्रगृह्या अचि नित्यम्}}, says a {{प्रगृह्य}} stays as it is before a vowel. So there is no sandhi.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's breath
source_body: Sūtra 8.2.66, {{ससजुषो रुः}}, turns a final {{स्}} into {{रु}}, and 8.3.15, {{खरवसानयोर्विसर्जनीयः}}, makes the {{र्}} a visarga at a pause. But 6.1.113, {{अतो रोरप्लुतादप्लुते}}, makes {{रु}} after {{अ}} into {{उ}} before a short {{अ}}, and 6.1.114, {{हशि च}}, does the same before a soft consonant.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's hiss
source_body: Sūtra 8.3.34, {{विसर्जनीयस्य सः}}, turns a visarga into {{स्}} before a hard consonant; 8.4.40, {{स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः}}, makes that {{स्}} into {{श्}} before {{च}}; and 8.4.41, {{ष्टुना ष्टुः}}, into {{ष्}} before {{ट}}. 8.3.35, {{शर्परे विसर्जनीयः}}, keeps it when a hard consonant is followed by a hiss.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's r and gone
source_body: The visarga is a changed {{रु}}, so after {{इ}} or {{उ}} the {{र्}} stays before a soft sound (8.2.66, 8.3.15). After {{अ}}, {{आ}}, 8.3.17, {{भोभगघपूर्वस्य योऽशि}}, makes it {{य्}} before a soft sound and 8.3.19, {{लोपः शाकल्यस्य}}, drops it. 6.1.132, {{एतत्तदोः सुलोपोऽकोरनञ्समासे हलि}}, drops the {{सु}} of {{सः}} and {{एषः}} before a consonant.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's voicing
source_body: Sūtra 8.2.39, {{झलां जशोऽन्ते}}, says that at the end of a word, any hard or aspirated stop ({{झल्}}) becomes the soft unaspirated stop ({{जश्}}) of its own class: {{त्}} becomes {{द्}}, {{क्}} becomes {{ग्}}. 8.4.53, {{झलां जश् झशि}}, does the same inside a word before a soft aspirate.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's place
source_body: Sūtra 8.4.40, {{स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः}}, says that {{स्}} or a dental ({{तवर्ग}}) next to a palatal ({{श्चु}}) becomes palatal. 8.4.41, {{ष्टुना ष्टुः}}, makes it cerebral next to a cerebral. Next to {{ल}}, 8.4.60, {{तोर्लि}}, makes {{त्}} into {{ल्}}.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's nose
source_body: Sūtra 8.4.45, {{यरोऽनुनासिकेऽनुनासिको वा}}, lets a stop before a nasal become the nasal of its class. 8.3.23, {{मोऽनुस्वारः}}, turns a final {{म्}} before a consonant into the dot. 8.4.58, {{अनुस्वारस्य ययि परसवर्णः}}, lets that dot take the nasal of the following class: {{संकल्पः}} or {{सङ्कल्पः}}.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini in reverse
source_body: Pāṇini's sūtras only join; the splitting is the reader's work, done by undoing each rule. {{अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः}} tells you a long {{आ}} may hide two {{अ/आ}}. {{आद्गुणः}} tells you {{ए}} may hide {{अ + इ}}. {{झलां जशोऽन्ते}} tells you a soft stop may be a hard one.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Reading order
source_body: After padaccheda comes {{अन्वयः}}, putting the words in prose order, and then the meaning. For now, you have the first step: you can see where every word begins and ends.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's pair
source_body: Sūtra 2.2.29, {{चार्थे द्वन्द्वः}}, says that words joined with the sense of {{च}} (and) form a {{द्वन्द्वः}}. 2.2.30, {{उपसर्जनं पूर्वम्}}, says the subordinate word goes first; and 2.1.22, {{तत्पुरुषः}}, 2.1.4, {{सह सुपा}}, say every compound is made by joining with the case endings.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's X's Y
source_body: Sūtra 2.1.22, {{तत्पुरुषः}}, names the class. 2.2.8, {{षष्ठी}}, makes the second case-pair for “of” into a compound: {{राज्ञः पुरुषः}} gives {{राजपुरुषः}}. And 2.1.24, {{द्वितीया श्रितातीतपतितगतात्यस्तप्राप्तापन्नैः}}, joins the second case with words like {{गत}}: {{ग्रामगतः}}.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's describing and counting
source_body: Sūtra 1.2.42, {{तत्पुरुषः समानाधिकरणः कर्मधारयः}}, calls a tatpuruṣa whose members share a case a {{कर्मधारयः}}; 2.1.57, {{विशेषणं विशेष्येण बहुलम्}}, joins a describing word to the described. 2.1.52, {{संख्यापूर्वो द्विगुः}}, calls a compound with a number first {{द्विगुः}}; 2.1.51 gives its sense of a group.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's not and maker
source_body: Sūtra 2.2.6, {{नञ्}}, joins {{नञ्}}, “not”, to the following word as a compound. 6.3.73, {{नलोपो नञः}}, drops its {{न्}}, and 6.3.74, {{तस्मान्नुडचि}}, adds {{न्}} before a vowel. For the maker, 2.2.19, {{उपपदमतिङ्}}, joins the word that stands next to a verb-noun, and 3.2.1, {{कर्मण्यण्}}, makes the doer: {{कुम्भकारः}}.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's “whose”
source_body: Sūtra 2.2.23, {{शेषो बहुव्रीहिः}}, calls the remaining compounds {{बहुव्रीहिः}}, and 2.2.24, {{अनेकमन्यपदार्थे}}, says several words join in the sense of another word, someone outside the compound. The compound's own gender and number come from the one it describes.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's adverb
source_body: Sūtra 2.1.5, {{अव्ययीभावः}}, names the class, and 2.1.6, {{अव्ययं विभक्तिसमीपसमृद्धिव्यृद्ध्यर्थाभावात्ययासम्प्रतिशब्दप्रादुर्भावपश्चाद्यथानुपूर्व्ययौगपद्यसादृश्यसम्पत्तिसाकल्यान्तवचनेषु}}, lists the senses in which an indeclinable joins a word. The result is {{अव्यय}} by 1.1.41, {{अव्ययीभावश्च}}.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's long compounds
source_body: Sūtra 2.1.3, {{प्राक् कडारात् समासः}}, says compounding is allowed before {{कडार}} in the order of the sūtras, which gives the grammar's own order of types. And 2.2.30, {{उपसर्जनं पूर्वम्}}, puts the subordinate member first. Long compounds are made by repeating the same rules.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's descendant
source_body: Sūtra 4.1.92, {{तस्यापत्यम्}}, gives a taddhita for “his descendant”; 4.1.83, {{प्राग्दीव्यतोऽण्}}, makes {{अण्}} the usual ending, and 7.2.117, {{तद्धितेष्वचामादेः}}, makes the first vowel grow. 4.1.95, {{अत इञ्}}, gives {{इञ्}} after {{अ}}-ending names ({{दाशरथिः}}), and 4.1.120, {{स्त्रीभ्यो ढक्}}, {{ढक्}} after feminines ({{कौन्तेयः}}).
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's state
source_body: Sūtra 5.1.119, {{तस्य भावस्त्वतलौ}}, gives {{त्व}} and {{तल्}} to a word to name its “being”. {{तल्}} makes a feminine in {{-ता}} by 4.1.4, and {{त्व}} a neuter. {{महत् + त्व}} doubles: {{महत्त्वम्}}.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's owner
source_body: Sūtra 5.2.94, {{तदस्यास्त्यस्मिन्निति मतुप्}}, gives {{मतुप्}} to say “he has it”; 8.2.9, {{मादुपधायाश्च मतोर्वोऽयवादिभ्यः}}, makes it {{वत्}} after a stem with {{म्}}, {{अ}} or {{आ}} before the end. For “related to”, 5.1.18, {{प्राग्वतेष्ठञ्}}, gives {{ठञ्}}, which 7.3.50, {{ठस्येकः}}, turns into {{इक}}.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's more and most
source_body: Sūtra 5.3.57, {{द्विवचनविभज्योपपदे तरबीयसुनौ}}, gives {{तरप्}} and {{ईयसुन्}} when comparing two; 5.3.55, {{अतिशायने तमबिष्ठनौ}}, gives {{तमप्}} and {{इष्ठन्}} for “most”. 6.4.157, {{प्रियस्थिरस्फिरोरुबहुलगुरुवृद्धतृप्रदीर्घवृन्दारकाणां प्रस्थस्फवर्बंहिगर्वर्षित्रब्द्राघिवृन्दाः}}, replaces the stem of a few adjectives: {{गुरु}} becomes {{गर्}}.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's pair
source_body: Pāṇini does not give a rule for the pair itself: it is part of how {{यद्}} and {{तद्}} are defined. {{यद्}} is {{सर्वनाम}}, taking the odd endings {{यस्मै}}, {{यस्मात्}}, {{यस्मिन्}} by 7.1.14 and 7.1.15; {{तद्}} answers it, and 7.2.106 gives {{सः}}.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's scene
source_body: Sūtra 2.3.37, {{यस्य च भावेन भावलक्षणम्}}, says that when one action marks the time of another, the first is put in the seventh case with its doer. 2.3.36, {{सप्तम्यधिकरणे च}}, gives the seventh case for the place or setting of an action.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's if
source_body: Sūtra 3.3.156, {{हेतुहेतुमतोर्लिङ्}}, gives {{लिङ्}} to both the condition and its result. 3.3.139, {{लिङ्निमित्ते लृङ् क्रियातिपत्तौ}}, gives {{लृङ्}} when the condition was not met. {{यदि}} and {{तर्हि}} are particles, {{निपात}}s, so they never change.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's order
source_body: Pāṇini does not fix a word order, because a case ending already says each word's job: 2.3.1, {{अनभिहिते}}, says a case is used for the relation not already expressed by the verb. So prose order is for the reader's comfort, and verse may use any order.
review_plan: Show the technical term or condition, a verified worked example and the limits of application. Use a derivation only where appropriate; do not turn every definition into a transformation.

title: Pāṇini's weights
source_body: Pāṇini defines the terms for his own use: 1.4.10, {{ह्रस्वं लघु}}, a short vowel is light; 1.4.11, {{संयोगे गुरु}}, a short vowel before a joined letter is heavy; 1.4.12, {{दीर्घं च}}, and a long vowel is heavy. The books of metre add the anusvāra and the visarga.

title: Pāṇini's names
source_body: Sūtra 1.1.71, {{आदिरन्त्येन सहेता}}, makes these names: a first letter, together with the last marker, stands for itself and the letters between. And 1.1.69, which you met with the vowels, lets each letter stand for its twins as well.

title: More markers
source_body: Other sūtras name markers at the start of a suffix: 1.3.6 {{षः प्रत्ययस्य}}, an initial {{ष्}}; 1.3.7 {{चुटू}}, an initial palatal or retroflex stop; 1.3.8 {{लशक्वतद्धिते}}, an initial {{ल्}}, {{श्}} or velar of a suffix that is not a taddhita.

title: Pāṇini's order
source_body: Sūtra 8.2.1, {{पूर्वत्रासिद्धम्}}, opens the last three quarters of the Aṣṭādhyāyī. From there, each rule counts as not yet applied when an earlier rule looks at the word, and when a rule before it in that part does. So the sound changes there wait until the end, and the order of the rules decides the word.
